title: Streaming Graph Neural Networks with Generative Replay

problem.claim: Incrementally updating GNNs for streaming graph data can produce outdated embeddings and degrade downstream performance.

gap.claim: Historical-data replay is constrained by storage limits, while incremental learning can suffer catastrophic forgetting.

contributions.claim: A streaming GNN uses generative replay to learn new patterns while maintaining existing knowledge without accessing historical data.
The model combines a main GNN with an auxiliary generative model that generates fake historical nodes and neighborhoods from random walks with restart.
Incremental update algorithms maintain the graph distribution in the generative model and current patterns in the GNN.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The model was evaluated on different streaming datasets.
The authors report that node classification results show efficient model updates and performance comparable to model retraining.
Code is reported as available in a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Streaming graph data makes inefficient incremental GNN updates harmful to embeddings and downstream performance.
Incremental learning forgets old knowledge, and storage limits restrict replay of historical graph data.
Generative replay uses an auxiliary model to produce fake historical samples for training the GNN alongside new data.
Separate incremental updates maintain the graph distribution and capture current patterns.
The authors evaluate streaming datasets and report efficient updates with node classification performance comparable to retraining.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the streaming datasets or experimental protocol.
The abstract does not provide quantitative results or efficiency measurements.
The abstract does not describe the generative model architecture or update algorithm in detail.
